description: Run an arbitrary Python callable as a Dagster asset -- Airflow PythonOperator / @task equivalent, with an optional Airflow-compatible execution context.

args.description: Static positional arguments passed to the callable.
args.label: Args

kwargs.label: Kwargs
kwargs.description: Static keyword arguments passed to the callable.

inputs.label: Inputs
inputs.description: {name: upstream_asset_key}. Each entry's value is loaded via the IO manager. `name` doubles as the Airflow task_id for `ti.xcom_pull(task_ids=name)`, and -- if the callable's signature declares a parameter called `name` -- is bound directly to it (TaskFlow-style). Keys must be valid Python identifiers.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

context_mode.label: Context Mode
context_mode.description: 'airflow' injects the Airflow-compatible context described above; 'none' calls the callable with just `args`/`kwargs`.

params.label: Params
params.description: Static dict exposed as `params` (mirrors Airflow's DAG-level params).

dag_run_conf_tag.label: Dag Run Conf Tag
dag_run_conf_tag.description: Run tag name carrying a JSON-encoded `dag_run.conf` dict -- set `dg launch --tags 'airflow/dag_run_conf={"key": "value"}'` (or your own tag name). Absent tag -> `{}`. Set to None/null to disable.

airflow_version.label: Airflow Version
airflow_version.description: Controls only `logical_date`: 2 (default) = partition interval start (Airflow 2's execution_date semantics -- the overwhelmingly common case for already-written DAGs). 3 = partition interval end (approximates Airflow 3's CronTriggerTimetable aligning logical_date with run_after; not a full timetable port). `data_interval_start`/`data_interval_end` are always the true interval regardless of this setting.

description.label: Description
description.description: Human-readable description surfaced in the Dagster UI.

timeout_seconds.label: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Unused by this component today (no built-in call timeout) -- kept for schema consistency with sibling infrastructure components.

partition_type.description: Enable partitioning: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly' for time-based; 'static' for a fixed set of values (e.g. customers); 'multi' for date × static (e.g. day × customer). Leave empty for unpartitioned.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: 0 (default): a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows. 1: include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the partitions definition (defaults to UTC).

partition_start.description: ISO date string for the first partition, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required for time-based and multi partition types.
partition_start.label: Partition Start Date

partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.
partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme_corp,globex,initech'. Required for static and multi types.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill execution strategy for a partitioned asset.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Policy Max Partitions Per Run

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)

freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule

on_missing_date.label: On Missing Date
on_missing_date.description: Only matters for context_mode='airflow' on an UN-PARTITIONED asset with no logical_date/data_interval_* run tags available (neither cron_schedule's/interval_schedule's add_logical_date_tag/add_interval_tags nor a partition window). 'warn' (default, preserves old behavior): logs a clear warning and falls back to datetime.now(utc) -- was previously SILENT, which is the bug this field fixes. 'fail': raises instead, for pipelines where a wrong date silently flowing into a query/filename would be worse than not running at all.

name: PythonCallableAsset
